summary: RFC 2648 defined the "ietf" URN namespace and some sub-namespaces, and RFC 3553 added "params" with its own registry. No single place listed every sub-namespace under "ietf". This document creates and fills such a registry, changing how new sub-namespaces are added.

plainLanguage.summary: A big list of names was scattered around. This makes one tidy list of every sub-name under "ietf" so nothing gets lost.

questions: second level urn namespaces under ietf
what is the ietf urn sub-namespaces registry
subtitle: A single IANA registry that lists every sub-namespace of the IETF URN namespace.

tldr.problem: No single registry listed all the sub-namespaces under the "ietf" URN namespace, which are spread across RFC 2648 and RFC 3553.
tldr.mechanism: It asks IANA to rename a registry group, add an "IETF URN Sub-namespaces" registry using IETF Review, and populate it with the seven existing entries.
tldr.outcome: New sub-namespaces under "ietf" now need IETF consensus, changing the mechanism from RFC 2648.

today: RFC 6924 is an Informational document that updates RFC 2648 and has not been obsoleted.

sections.title: The Missing Registry
sections.content:
RFC 2648 defines the "ietf" URN namespace and several sub-namespaces. RFC 3553 adds the "params" sub-namespace and a registry for allocations under it. But no registry listed, in one place, all sub-namespaces of "ietf".

This document creates and populates one, which changes the mechanism RFC 2648 defined for adding new sub-namespaces. It updates RFC 2648.
sections.plainLanguage: Some names lived in one book and some in another. Now there is one master list.

sections.title: The Three IANA Actions
sections.content: IANA took three actions. First, it renamed the group "IETF Protocol Parameter Identifiers" to "Uniform Resource Name (URN) Namespace for IETF Use"; the existing params registry stays, and its procedure became IETF Review (formerly called IETF Consensus). Second, it added a new registry, "IETF URN Sub-namespaces", listed first in the group, with IETF Review as the policy from RFC 5226. Third, it populated that registry.
sections.plainLanguage: The librarians renamed a shelf, added a new master list at the front, and wrote the names into it.

sections.title: What the Registry Lists
sections.content:
The registry is the official one for sub-namespaces of the IETF URN namespace. It holds seven entries: rfc, fyi, std, bcp, id and mtg, all from RFC 2648 with no separate IANA registry, and params from RFC 3553 with its own IANA registry.

The security section says this is a procedural document entirely unrelated to security.
sections.plainLanguage: The list has seven names, and only one of them has its own sign-in book.
